simple.meaning: לוּבִי (Lûwbîy) is a Hebrew word meaning “a Libyan or inhabitant of interior Africa (only in plural).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: לוּבִי (H3864) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 2 Chronicles 12:3, with occurrences in 2 Chronicles, Daniel, Nahum.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to לוּבִי (H3864) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in לוּבִי (H3864) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: לוּבִי (Lûwbîy) / H3864 is traced through 2 Chronicles 12:3, 2 Chronicles 16:8, Daniel 11:43, Nahum 3:9 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: a Libyan or inhabitant of interior Africa (only in plural)
definitions.full: H3864. Lubim [ לוּב ], לֻבִֿים לוּבִים, name, of a people, plural Lybians , in North Africa, west of Egypt; — Nahum 3:9 ( + מּוּט ), 2Chr 12:3 ( ᵐ5 Λιβυες ; + כּוּשִׁים סֻכִּיִּים, מִצְרַיִם, ), 16:8 ᵐ5 Λιβυες ; (+ כּוּוִים ); לֻבִֿים Dan 11:43 (see Baer; with כֻּשִֿׁים מִצְרַיִם, ), Theod. Λιβυων ; probably = לְהָבִים (q. v.) Gen 10:13 = 1Chr 1:11 A ᵐ5 L Λαβιειμ ; read לוּבים perhaps also Jer 46:9 (for HCT לוּדִים , compare Sta Javan 5f. ), ᵐ5 Λυδοι ( מּוּט ib. = Λιβυες ); ᵐ5 Sm Co Sta Javan 6 Berthol read לוּב Ezek 30:5 (for HCT כּוּב , q. v.) See WMM As.Eur.115 .
definitions.rootNote: or לֻבִּי ; (Daniel 11:43), partrial from a name probably derived from an unused root meaning to thirst, i.e. a dry region; apparently

occurrences.englishText: with twelve hundred chariots, and sixty thousand horsemen. The people were without number who came with him out of Egypt: the Lubim, the Sukkiim, and the Ethiopians.
Weren’t the Ethiopians and the Lubim a huge army, with chariots and exceedingly many horsemen? Yet, because you relied on Yahweh, he delivered them into your hand.
But he will have power over the treasures of gold and of silver, and over all the precious things of Egypt. The Libyans and the Ethiopians will be at his steps.
Cush and Egypt were her boundless strength. Put and Libya were her helpers.
